prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Stronger for Scotland: The SNP’s 2015 manifesto vows to make Scotland’s voice louder at Westminster and deliver a progressive alternative to austerity. A vote for the SNP is a vote to end damaging cuts, invest in jobs and services, protect the NHS, raise wages, and oppose new nuclear weapons. The SNP will never put the Tories into power; if there is an anti‑Tory majority, it will work with others to keep them out and push Labour to deliver real change.

Economy and public finances: The SNP proposes modest, responsible increases in public spending each year, with borrowing and debt falling as a share of national income. Priorities include major infrastructure investment, a northern focus (HS2 to and from Scotland, better broadband/4G with a Universal Service Obligation), green energy and housing. Tax fairness will see the 50p top rate restored, a bank levy and bankers’ bonus tax, a mansion tax, a crackdown on avoidance, abolition of non‑dom status, and review of pensions tax relief for the wealthiest. The party backs a sovereign wealth/energy fund. It will seed‑capitalise a Scottish Business Development Bank, improve SME finance and prompt payment rules, devolve and halve Air Passenger Duty then abolish it, consider a VAT cut for hospitality, raise the Employment Allowance to £6,000, and reintroduce a post‑study work visa.

Jobs, pay and welfare: The minimum wage will rise to £8.70 by 2020 (with higher youth and apprentice rates), alongside a UK‑wide push for the Living Wage and action on exploitative zero‑hours contracts. The SNP will uprate benefits at least with the cost of living, increase Universal Credit work allowances, scrap the Bedroom Tax, halt and replace UC/PIP rollout (reversing DLA to PIP), reform sanctions and disability assessments, and raise Carer’s Allowance to match JSA.

Public services and household support: The SNP will protect the NHS from privatisation and deliver £2 billion extra for Scotland by 2020‑21. Free childcare will expand to 30 hours a week for all 3–4 year‑olds and eligible 2‑year‑olds; 30,000 Modern Apprenticeships and expanded EMA will support young people; university tuition remains free. It backs a UK target of 100,000 affordable homes annually and action to cut energy bills by funding ECO from general taxation, enforcing wholesale price pass‑through, and ending prepayment penalties.

Security, defence and the environment: The SNP opposes Trident renewal and any new nuclear weapons, redirecting savings to health and education, while strengthening Scotland’s conventional capabilities and veterans’ support. It backs a moratorium on fracking, ambitious carbon targets, support for offshore/onshore wind, hydro and CCS, community energy and grid reform, and a stronger, borrowing‑enabled Green Investment Bank.

Democracy, rights and culture: The SNP seeks STV for Commons elections, abolition of the House of Lords, votes at 16, robust recall, protected privacy (no “snoopers’ charter”), stronger equality (50% women on public boards, equal pay audits, tighter maternity protections), removal of VAT on sanitary products, devolved broadcasting and a fair BBC Scotland share to boost the creative sector.

Europe and the world: The SNP opposes EU withdrawal and demands a double‑majority referendum rule; it seeks a greater devolved role in EU decision‑making, support for the European Arrest Warrant, and a TTIP exemption for public services. It supports the 0.7% aid target with quality safeguards, recognition of Palestine alongside Israel, and a UK LGBTI rights envoy.

Home Rule: Deliver Smith in full, then go further to full fiscal responsibility. Priorities for immediate devolution include employment policy (minimum wage), welfare, business taxes, National Insurance and equality powers, with Barnett retained during transition.

The SNP offers an investment‑led, fair, green alternative to austerity—making Scotland stronger at Westminster and delivering progressive change across the UK.
